en: The Hymn to the Support of the Hands of Śrī Pārvatī and Śaṅkara.
O Śambhu, Lord of the protection of the glorious world of moving and unmoving beings; O thousand-faced one, cause of the three classes of attendants;
O bestower of prosperity, equal to forgiveness, perfectly tranquil, and worshipped by the lords of the gods; O Śrī Pārvatīśa, grant me the support of Your hand.
O You whose nature is eternal and unimpeded, who possess a host of great and powerful deities, whose true form is truth, and whose compassionate disposition is peerless.
O Śrīpāda... whose intellect is free from world-weariness, O you of celebrated and vast fame!

... 2 O Śambhu, whose hand holds the noose, the goad, and the gesture of fearlessness, who destroys the thick mass of those who bow before you, whose conduct is skillful, whose plowshare is vast throughout the universe, and who has conquered the hosts of Rākṣasas with the points of your trident—O Śrīpāda... 3
May there be the birth of a mouse-eating crow and the like for those devoted to extreme sin, and may such a sinful birth be mine;
and for one whose mind was pure in childhood yet who was devoid of discernment, may there be [the state of] Śrīpā...
(4) May heaven be attained through dogs with feet smeared with knowledge, and through children with clever hearts, and through fruits.
O Śrīpāda... [for one] whose behavior is like that of a restless child due to ignorance.
(5) O Śrīpāda... [for one] blinded by the intoxication of youth, whose vision is clouded, who has offered his heart to two births, and who is devoted to young women with firm, rounded breasts. (6)

For one whose heart is bound by ignorance and who, intent on acquiring wealth, is engaged in various sinful reflections, [there is the bondage] of wife and sons through the snare of greed for the riches of the earth-dwellers; may Śrī Pā... protect them. 7.
For one whose mind is arrogant, thinking, "This wife is mine, these children are mine, and this grain is mine," [there is such bondage].
Of that evil-souled one, intent on wicked deeds, [may] Śrīpāda... 8.

When old age has arrived, or when afflicted by phlegm-diseases, wind, bile, thirst, and the like, he cries out to his own wife and children, "Give me food, give me clothing!"—of such a purifier, [may] Śrīpāda... 9.
In childhood, one is intent on playing; in youth, one is addicted to women; and when decrepit and sharing the portion of old age, one is intent on anxiety.
When wisdom has perished, O Śrīpāda...

at that time, amidst the cries of "Alas! Alas! from the wife, children, and kinsmen who have become like the waters of the ocean, with their wretched words of lamentation, [the servant] is supported by his master.

O Śrī Nīlakaṇṭha, when one has fallen into wretchedness and is tormented by the messengers of Yama—those terrifying messengers of Yama who arrive with faces formidable with fangs and bearing the staff of Yama—who then protects him? O Śarva, Lord of the Universe, who is his protector then? 12
"Come, you who are devoted to sin!"—so saying, the messengers of Yama bind him by the neck with cruel nooses;

seizing his hands and feet while he is under their control, they [drag him away]. O Śrīpā... 13 ...he speaks and weeps, looking at his sons, unable to utter the divine name due to the power of the *vaidhṛti* yoga.
Out of fear, Śrīpāda...

[remembers] him who was led by those messengers of Yama—who were accompanied by their followers—to a place devoid of water for his wicked deeds, thick with the thorns of *sikatā* (sand) and wretched stones, a ground scorched by the intense heat of a sun that provides no shade. 14–15.

O compassionate Śrīpāda... at that time, out of pity for me who had fallen into calamity, you went [to help], disregarding the multitude of my vices as your servant; I was terrified and held in the power of the messengers. 16.
For one who has come seeking refuge, there is truly no likeness to the virtues of wife, son, or kin, except for that [protection] belonging to the Son of the Sun (Yama).
Even when followed by messengers, there was extreme fear for him who had gone... Śrīpā... 17.
Having committed great sins since birth, which cause the cycle of existence through the blinding darkness of pride, O Lord, your name has never been taken by me... Śrīpā... 18.
O Lord, friend of the distressed, protector of those with sincere devotion, O Śivāramaṇa, for me, your servant—
at the time of the body’s end— having bestowed Your name upon me, [may] Śrīpā... 19 ...there is no other boon from the God, O Girijeśa, ocean of compassion, except for the cessation of non-existence.

Having bestowed upon me a most auspicious mindfulness of your name, O Śrīpāda... 20 And when death is indeed imminent, if I should fall into a state of mind devoid of mindfulness, then, O Umādhava, protect me as you have arrived; O Śrīpāda... 21

If, due to the floods of sins acquired in the past through immeasurable hardships, I were to meet death in the forest wilderness as if in my own city—O Śrīpāda, it is not known when You might become gracious toward me.
For one who meets an untimely death by means of tigers, lions, deer, snakes, water, fire, wind, thieves, disease, and so forth; 22. Śārdūlavikrīḍita.
Having instructed him who had arrived there in this [teaching] called Amṛta, Śrīpā...
॥ 23 ॥ O Śrī Maṅgirīśa, O Moon-crested One, O Divine Form, O Supporter of Śrī Pārvatī, O Lord primarily served by the Consort of Ramā;
O Dispeller of all obstacles, O Wielder of the Noose, O Lord, for me Śrīpā... ॥ 24 ॥
This hymn, which is the eternal support of the hand of the Great Śiva, was composed by the most excellent of great teachers, Śiva-Śaṅkara;

for Śambhu bestows all desired boons upon one who recites it every morning at dawn. He who, being self-restrained, recites this "Support of the Hand" hymn of the Lord of Śrī Pārvatī in the early morning—
But at his death, one should grant him mindfulness here; for Śrī Pārvatīśa indeed grants the support of His hand.
Thus ends the *Śrīpārvatīśakarāvalamba-stotra*, composed by the venerable Paramahaṃsa Parivrājaka, Śrī Śaṅkarabhāratī Svāmī.
